title: How to Add a Realistic Shadow to Product Photos (Makes Them Look Professional Instantly)
description: A subtle shadow makes floating products look grounded and premium. Here's how to add realistic shadows without Photoshop.

blocks.text: Pure white backgrounds are great for marketplaces. But they can make products look like they're floating in space—unnatural and cheap. A subtle drop shadow anchors your product and adds instant premium polish.

Shadow Style by Product Type
Small products (jewelry, cosmetics): Soft, close shadow directly below. Subtle.
Medium products (bottles, boxes): Slightly angled shadow at 45°. More visible.
Large products (furniture, appliances): Wide, soft shadow spreading behind. Grounded.
Floating/hanging products (clothing): Minimal or no shadow. Product should float intentionally.
Match your shadow to your product's implied weight and physics.
Common Shadow Mistakes
Too dark. Black shadows look cartoon-like. Use dark gray at 30-50% opacity max.
Too sharp. Real shadows have soft edges. Never use hard-line shadows unless mimicking direct sunlight.
Wrong angle. All products in your catalog should have shadows from the same angle. Otherwise it looks like they were shot in different studios.
Too big. Shadows should be smaller than the product itself. Massive shadows look fake.
